sources.reason: The ai-close-work-item target accepts TASK but drops ARGS, which removed the required --worktree argument from the real recovery invocation.
The closure implementation derives the work branch from the current checkout rather than proving that the requested task maps to that branch, allowing task/PR receipt disagreement.
Lifecycle tests cover the direct parser path but did not prove the Makefile forwards --worktree or reject task/branch mismatches.
The preserved local diagnostic receipt proves the mismatch: task #474 is paired with PR #476 and the executor branch. It must never be treated as valid closure evidence.

rawUserRequest: Continue: fix the discovered workflow defect before proceeding. The explicit worktree closure for #474 must be safe and must not repeat the task/branch mismatch.

declaredIntent.summary: Prevent dropped closure selectors and task-to-branch evidence mismatches before any provider or branch-cleanup action.

riskAssessment.reason: Closure can delete branches. A dropped --worktree argument and a task/current-branch mismatch create misleading receipts and could clean up the wrong Work Item. The fix must fail before provider calls, receipt generation, or deletion whenever task, branch, or explicit target do not agree.

The closure CLI verifies the requested Work Item ID maps to the branch checked out in the selected worktree before provider queries, receipt generation, synchronization, or branch deletion.

guidelines: The Makefile must forward only declared command arguments and must not silently drop a safety-critical target selector.
Requested task identity, selected worktree branch, provider PR, and Closure Receipt must remain one evidence-bound chain; mismatch fails closed before mutation.
Do not alter or delete the invalid local diagnostic receipt; it is evidence of the process defect, not closure evidence.
Document the exceptional recovery command consistently in English and Japanese without weakening normal closure behavior.

intent.problem: The first real #474 recovery invocation exposed two linked lifecycle defects: Makefile silently discarded ARGS so --worktree never reached the CLI, and the CLI allowed the requested task archive to diverge from the checked-out Work Item branch. It consequently rendered a local receipt labelled #474 but bound it to PR #476 and the executor branch. #474 itself remains open for correct lifecycle closure.
constraints: Do not treat the mismatched local receipt as valid closure evidence or delete it; retain it as diagnostic evidence.
Do not close, delete, or rewrite #474 evidence until the corrected path is merged and re-executed.
Retain default closure behavior and all existing merged PR, Head SHA, base synchronization, Receipt, and deletion gates.
A mismatch must fail before any provider lookup, receipt write, base switch, or local/remote branch mutation.
The Makefile and the English/Japanese lifecycle documentation must agree on the actual argument-passing command.
intent.rationale: Explicit cross-worktree selection is safety-critical. It is useful only when the requested Work Item, selected worktree branch, provider PR, and resulting receipt are one deterministic evidence chain. Forwarding the selector and proving that identity before work begins turns a latent misleading-cleanup path into a fail-closed rejection.
